name: Cheung pessary trial
question: Does adding a vaginal pessary to pelvic floor exercise training improve symptoms and quality of life in women with symptomatic pelvic organ prolapse?

arms.label: Vaginal pessary plus pelvic floor exercise training

design.population: Previously untreated women with symptomatic stage I–III pelvic organ prolapse.
design.locator: Full text, Methods, p 74; Table 1, p 77

verdictNote: Prolapse distress improved at 6 and 12 months; prolapse impact differed at 12 months only.
takeaway: In previously untreated women with symptomatic stage I–III prolapse, adding a ring pessary to pelvic floor exercise training improved prolapse distress at 6 and 12 months and prolapse impact at 12 months versus training alone; 83/139 (60%) retained the pessary at 12 months.

reports.label: 12-month primary report
reports.dateLocator: Europe PMC firstPublicationDate; PubMed print issue July 2016
reports.citation: Cheung RYK, Lee JHS, Lee LL, et al. "Vaginal Pessary in Women With Symptomatic Pelvic Organ Prolapse: A Randomized Controlled Trial." *Obstet Gynecol.* 2016;128(1):73-80. doi:10.1097/AOG.0000000000001489
reports.followUpLocator: Full text, Methods and Results, pp 74–75

results.endpoint: Prolapse symptom distress at 6 and 12 months
results.measure: 6-month median POPDI score (interquartile range) and 12-month mean change, intention-to-treat with missing scores imputed
results.note: Both time points met the 5% threshold: 6-month median-score P=0.02; 12-month mean-change P<0.01. At 12 months, median scores were 32.1 (IQR 12.5–78.6) versus 49.4 (21.4–95.2), P=0.04. Between-arm 12-month change difference −25.0 points is arithmetic. At 12 months, 86/139 (62%) versus 48/137 (35%) achieved the minimal important difference (P<0.01).
results.locator: Full text, Results, pp 75–77; Table 2, p 78

results.endpoint: Prolapse impact on quality of life
results.measure: 12-month mean change in POPIQ score, intention-to-treat with missing scores imputed
results.note: Between-arm change difference −32.5 points is arithmetic; the reported P<0.01 is for the between-group comparison. At 12 months, median scores were 0.3 (IQR 0–22.2) versus 8.9 (0–64.9), P=0.02. At 12 months, 49/139 (35%) versus 23/137 (16.8% calculated; article prints 18%) achieved the minimal important difference (P=0.01).
results.locator: Full text, Results, pp 75–77; Table 2, p 78

results.endpoint: Prolapse impact on quality of life at 6 months
results.measure: 6-month median POPIQ score (interquartile range), intention-to-treat with imputation
12-month improvement among questionnaire completers; adjusted logistic regression

harms.label: Vaginal bleeding, discharge, and infection

values.exp: Bleeding 9/132 (6.8%); bothersome discharge 6/132 (4.5%); bacterial vaginosis 1 woman

harms.note: Bleeding P=0.17 and discharge P=0.16; the single vaginal infection in the pessary arm required antibiotics. Infection denominator was not specified separately.
harms.locator: Full text, Results and Table 3, pp 77–78

harms.label: De novo urinary symptoms

values.exp: Stress incontinence 24/50 (48.0%); urge incontinence 17/73 (23.3%); voiding difficulty 10/92 (10.9%)
values.ctl: Stress incontinence 13/58 (22.4%); urge incontinence 19/84 (22.6%); voiding difficulty 8/97 (8.2%)

harms.note: Denominators exclude women with the corresponding symptom at baseline; between-group P values 0.01, 0.85, and 0.54, respectively.

delivery.label: Completed 12-month follow-up
delivery.note: Questionnaire completers; primary outcome analysis imputed missing values for 7/139 pessary and 9/137 control participants at 12 months (Table 2).

delivery.label: Ring pessary fitting and retention

values.exp: Successfully fitted and comfortable 92/139 (66%) at 2 weeks; retained 87/139 (63%) at 6 months and 83/139 (60%) at 12 months
values.ctl: No pessary; 120/137 (88%) remained on conservative treatment at 12 months

delivery.note: Largest comfortable ring pessary inserted; slipped pessaries could be refitted with the same or next size up to three times. Across arms, 61 women received a treatment different from allocation by 12 months.
delivery.locator: Full text, Methods, p 74; Results, p 75; Discussion, p 79

delivery.label: Pelvic floor exercise training and adherence

values.exp: Regular exercise 53/135 (39.3% calculated; article prints 39.2%) at 6 months; 72/135 (53.3%) at 12 months
values.ctl: Regular exercise 66/134 (49.3%) at 6 months; 56/130 (43.1%) at 12 months

delivery.note: Both arms received a teaching session within 2 weeks and individual sessions at weeks 4, 8, and 16. They were advised to practice daily with at least two sets of 8–12 repetitions per day and 8–10 exercises per session at least twice weekly. Reported adherence was at least twice daily on 3 days per week; between-arm P=0.10 at both follow-ups.
delivery.locator: Full text, Methods, p 74; Results, p 75
